title: Archer Moving Averages Trends (AMAT)
summary: Flags a bar as trending only when a fast and a slow exponential average agree on both their order and their direction, and measures their spread.
description:
AMAT asks two exponential moving averages, a fast one and a slow one, whether they agree. Both start from the first value of the source and follow the usual exponential recursion with a weight of `2 / (period + 1)`.

A bar is an uptrend bar, drawn as a column of +1, when the fast average is above the slow one and both averages rose on this bar. It is a downtrend bar, a column of -1, when the fast average is below the slow one and both fell. Every other bar is 0: the averages are in one order but at least one of them is moving the other way, so the trend is not confirmed.

The second line, **Trend Strength %**, is the distance between the two averages as a percentage of the slow average. It grows as the averages pull apart and shrinks as they converge, whichever side is on top.
howToRead:
Green columns at +1 mark bars where the uptrend is confirmed by both order and slope, red columns at -1 mark confirmed downtrend bars, and a flat zero means the averages disagree. A long unbroken run of one colour is a clean trend; a mix of zeros and short runs is a market without direction.

Use the strength line to judge how established a trend is. A rising strength line with steady columns shows the averages separating, while a falling one warns that they are converging and a crossing may follow. Both readings come from moving averages, so they confirm a move after it starts rather than predicting it.

settings.label: Fast Period
settings.description: Length of the fast exponential average. A shorter length reacts sooner and breaks the trend state more often.

settings.label: Slow Period
settings.description: Length of the slow exponential average. A longer length makes the trend state steadier and the strength readings larger.

settings.label: Source
settings.description: The price series both averages follow, the close by default.

faq.q: Why is the value zero when the fast average is clearly above the slow one?
faq.a: A trend bar also needs both averages to be moving in the trend's direction on that bar. If either one ticked the other way, the bar is reported as 0 until they agree again.

faq.q: Does the strength line show direction?
faq.a: No. It is the absolute spread as a percentage of the slow average, so it never drops below zero while the slow average is above zero. Read the direction from the columns.

faq.q: Why does the first bar show no trend?
faq.a: Both averages and their previous values start at the first source value, so on that bar they are equal and neither the order nor the slope test can pass.
